symbols.role: Alternative-world kernel after abduction on one factual transition.

assumptions.condition: Every positive nominal transition cell satisfies \(P(y\mid x,a)\ge\epsilon\).
The response programs \(F_1,\ldots,F_T\) are independent and identically distributed with common law \(q\).
The response-program sequence \(F_{1:T}\) is independent of \(X_0\).
The factual and alternative worlds start from the same unit-level state: \(Z_0=X_0\).

standard.name: SCM consistency under shared exogenous state

assumptions.condition: The target kernel admits the Poisson equation \(r-g\mathbf 1=h-K_{\pi}h\).
The Poisson solution satisfies \(\operatorname{span}(h)=\max_z h(z)-\min_z h(z)\le B\).
The rowwise multinomial calibration sample used to form \(\widehat P\) is independent of \(E_T\).

standard.name: independent sample splitting for set-valued inference

definitions.name: Stationary compatible response-SCM class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_{d,k,T}(\epsilon,B)=\{(P,q,\rho,b,\pi,o,r,g,h): q\in\Theta(P),\ F_{1:T}\text{ satisfies the iid-response and initial-exogeneity conditions},\ Z_0=X_0,\ P\text{ satisfies positive-cells},\ r-g\mathbf 1=h-K_{\pi}h,\ \operatorname{span}(h)\le B\}\).

definitions.name: Shared-response factual and counterfactual trajectories
definitions.construction: Draw \(X_0\sim\rho\), set \(Z_0=X_0\), draw \(F_t\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}q\), and recursively set \(X_t=F_t(X_{t-1},b(X_{t-1}))\) and \(Z_t=F_t(Z_{t-1},\pi(Z_{t-1}))\) for \(t=1,\ldots,T\); report \(E_T=(o(X_0),\ldots,o(X_T))\).

definitions.name: Induced factual-record law
definitions.construction: For every \((u_0,\ldots,u_T)\in\mathcal O^{T+1}\), define \[\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}(E_T=(u_0,\ldots,u_T))=\sum_{s_{0:T}\in\mathcal S^{T+1}}\rho(s_0)\prod_{t=1}^T P(s_t\mid s_{t-1},b(s_{t-1}))\prod_{t=0}^T\mathbf 1\{o(s_t)=u_t\}.\] This law is common to every \(q\in\Theta(P)\).

definitions.name: Sharp coarsened-record stationary-response interval
definitions.construction: For every \(e\in\mathcal O^{T+1}\) with \(\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}(E_T=e)>0\), define \(I_T(P,\rho,b,o,e)=\{Q_{q,T}(P,\rho,b,o,e):q\in\Theta(P)\}=[\min_{q\in\Theta(P)}Q_{q,T}(P,\rho,b,o,e),\max_{q\in\Theta(P)}Q_{q,T}(P,\rho,b,o,e)]\) and \(D_T(P,\rho,b,o,e)=\max_{q\in\Theta(P)}Q_{q,T}(P,\rho,b,o,e)-\min_{q\in\Theta(P)}Q_{q,T}(P,\rho,b,o,e)\).

definitions.name: Full-record conditional target and sharp interval
definitions.construction: For every \(x_{0:T}\in\mathcal S^{T+1}\) with \(\rho(x_0)\prod_{t=1}^T P(x_t\mid x_{t-1},b(x_{t-1}))>0\), define \(Q^{\mathrm{full}}_{q,T}(x_{0:T})=\mathbb E_{q,\rho,b,\pi}[T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^T r(Z_t)\mid X_{0:T}=x_{0:T}]\), \(I^{\mathrm{full}}_T(P,\rho,b,x_{0:T})=\{Q^{\mathrm{full}}_{q,T}(x_{0:T}):q\in\Theta(P)\}\), and \(D^{\mathrm{full}}_T(P,\rho,b,x_{0:T})=\sup I^{\mathrm{full}}_T(P,\rho,b,x_{0:T})-\inf I^{\mathrm{full}}_T(P,\rho,b,x_{0:T})\).

definitions.name: Stationary shared-response endpoint program
definitions.construction: For coarsened evidence \(e\), enumerate factual-state paths compatible with \(e\) and alternative-state paths; at every date multiply the same stationary selector \(q_f\) through the factor \(\sum_{f\in\mathcal R}q_f\mathbf 1\{f(x_{t-1},b(x_{t-1}))=x_t,\ f(z_{t-1},\pi(z_{t-1}))=z_t\}\), sum all hidden paths, divide by \(\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}(E_T=e)\), and minimize or maximize the resulting conditional reward over \(q\in\Theta(P)\).

definitions.name: Conditional Poisson martingale family
definitions.construction: For each \(q\in\Theta(P)\), propagate \(\alpha_t(q)\), form \(\Delta_t(q)=\alpha_{t-1}(q)\{L_q(X_{t-1},X_t)-K_{\pi}\}h\), and set \(M_T(q)=\sum_{t=1}^T\Delta_t(q)\); control the whole family by a self-normalized face decomposition using predictable quadratic variation rather than a likelihood-denominator lower bound.

definitions.name: Legal full-support binary feedback witness
definitions.construction: In coordinate order \((0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1)\), take \(\mathcal S=\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), \(X_0=Z_0=0\), \(b\equiv0\), \(\pi\equiv1\), let \(o\) be the identity map, let \(r(z)=z\), take nominal one-probabilities \(p_{\mathrm{bin}}\), and use the response laws \(q_0,\nu_+,\nu_-,q_+,q_-\) declared above. This tuple is \(\mathfrak W_{\mathrm{bin}}\).

definitions.name: Synchronizer--two-permutation kill-test handle
definitions.construction: For the explicitly declared uniform binary-row recursion \(m_t(\lambda,\vartheta)\), apply a two-parameter self-normalized martingale covering with corner-integrable derivative energy to \(\sup_{(\lambda,\vartheta)\in[0,1]^2}|\sum_{t=1}^T m_t(\lambda,\vartheta)|\); if this control fails, search for a horizon-dependent parameter sequence attaining the divergent normalized width.

definitions.name: Simultaneous multinomial transition region
definitions.construction: Define \(\mathcal C_{\alpha}\) as the set of controlled kernels \(P'\) with the known zero pattern, \(P'(y\mid x,a)\ge\epsilon\) on positive cells, \(|P'(y\mid x,a)-\widehat P(y\mid x,a)|\le\delta_{x,a}\) for every cell, and some \((g',h')\) satisfying \(r-g'\mathbf 1=h'-K'_{\pi}h'\) and \(\operatorname{span}(h')\le B\).

definitions.name: Honest confidence fiber
definitions.construction: If \(\mathcal C_{\alpha}\neq\varnothing\), set \(\widehat I_{T,\alpha}(P,\rho,b,o,e)=\operatorname{hull}(\bigcup_{P'\in\mathcal C_{\alpha}}I_T(P',\rho,b,o,e))\); if \(\mathcal C_{\alpha}=\varnothing\), set \(\widehat I_{T,\alpha}(P,\rho,b,o,e)=[0,1]\). The known zero pattern ensures that every \(e\) positive under \(\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}\) is positive under each retained \(\Pr_{P',\rho,b,o}\).

statements.statement: As the first D0 obligation, determine whether the synchronizer--two-permutation square satisfies \[\sup_{T\ge1}T^{-1/2}\mathbb E\sup_{(\lambda,\vartheta)\in[0,1]^2}\left|\sum_{t=1}^T m_t(\lambda,\vartheta)\right|<\infty.\] An affirmative answer must give a bound uniform on the entire two-parameter square and then determine whether its predictable-scale argument localizes over every face of \(\Theta(P)\) to prove \[\mathbb E_{\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}}\sup_{q\in\Theta(P)}|M_T(q)|\le \frac{511B d^{dk}}{\epsilon}\sqrt T\quad\text{for every }T\ge1.\] A negative answer must give an explicit horizon-dependent \(\lambda_T,\vartheta_T\) counterselection and derive the sharp replacement rate for \(\mathbb E_{\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}}D_T(P,\rho,b,o,E_T)\) on the unchanged model class.
statements.justification: The two-parameter square is the smallest unsolved interior face and the mandatory falsification test for the whole-polytope parametric rate.
statements.gap: HaughSingal2026Casino, arXiv version 3, pages 9--11, Sections 4.2--4.3, shows only that in its special casino model the time-homogeneous and time-inhomogeneous \(\mathrm{EWAC}/T\) bounds converge together as \(T\to\infty\); it gives neither a finite root-\(T\) rate nor a bound uniform over the complete finite-state stationary response-program fiber. deLaPenaLaiShao2009 and RakhlinSridharanTewari2015 provide general maximal-inequality tools but do not evaluate this posterior-normalized response-polytope family at vanishing response masses.
statements.consumer: The result either supplies the first uniform ingredient for the conditional root-rate theorem or identifies the sharp slower headline rate through a legal face of the same causal model.

statements.statement: For every \((P,q,\rho,b,\pi,o,r,g,h)\in\mathfrak M_{d,k,T}(\epsilon,B)\) and every \(e\in\mathcal O^{T+1}\) satisfying \(\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}(E_T=e)>0\), the stationary shared-response endpoint program returns exactly \(I_T(P,\rho,b,o,e)\). Its minimum and maximum are attained by \(q^-,q^+\in\Theta(P)\), with the same response-mass vector reused at every date and on every hidden branch.
statements.justification: This supporting proposition fixes the stationary shared-selector optimization object used by the rate and confidence statements.
statements.gap: ZhangTianBareinboim2022PartialCounterfactual supplies generic finite canonical-SCM optimization, and HaughSingal2023DynamicLatent uses time-invariant response distributions; the proposition records only the shared stationary-response specialization needed here and is not presented as a separate novelty claim.
statements.consumer: The rate analysis and calibration-set inversion use attained endpoints of one response law shared across dates.

statements.statement: For every \(e\in\mathcal O^{T+1}\) with \(\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}(E_T=e)>0\), \[D_T(P,\rho,b,o,e)\le\mathbb E_{\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}}\!\left[D^{\mathrm{full}}_T(P,\rho,b,X_{0:T})\mid E_T=e\right].\] Consequently, \[\mathbb E_{\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}}D_T(P,\rho,b,o,E_T)\le\mathbb E_{\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}}D^{\mathrm{full}}_T(P,\rho,b,X_{0:T}).\]
statements.justification: This moves arbitrary state coarsening to a conditional averaging step without applying a full-record functional to an observation record or assuming filter contraction.
statements.gap: OberstSontag2019 samples one selected POMDP mechanism, and vanHandel2009 studies stability within a fixed hidden model; neither compares coarsened and full-record envelopes over all compatible response mechanisms.
statements.consumer: Users with privacy-coarsened or latent factual records inherit any full-record expected-width certificate.

statements.statement: After shifting \(h\) to have range in \([0,B]\), each \(\Delta_t(q)\) is a martingale difference under \(\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}\), its conditional range has length at most \(B\), and for every \(q\in\Theta(P)\) the exact full-record identity \[T\{Q^{\mathrm{full}}_{q,T}(X_{0:T})-g\}=\alpha_0(q)K_{\pi}h-\alpha_T(q)K_{\pi}h+M_T(q)\] holds \(\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}\)-almost surely.
statements.justification: The identity isolates full-record ambiguity in a posterior-normalized martingale family with a uniformly bounded terminal bias.
statements.gap: SayedanaCainesMahajan2025 derives the analogous decomposition and concentration for one fixed MDP kernel, not a supremum over a record-adaptive compatible-response polytope whose masses may vanish.
statements.consumer: The decomposition supplies the proof interface for the square kill test and any whole-polytope rate inequality.

statements.statement: Conditional on an affirmative resolution of \texttt{oeq:polytope-maximal-inequality} establishing \[\mathbb E_{\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}}\sup_{q\in\Theta(P)}|M_T(q)|\le \frac{511B d^{dk}}{\epsilon}\sqrt T\] uniformly over \(\mathfrak M_{d,k,T}(\epsilon,B)\), every \(T\ge1\), initial law \(\rho\), and deterministic observation map \(o\) satisfy \[\mathbb E_{\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}}[D_T(P,\rho,b,o,E_T)]\le\min\left\{1,\frac{C_{d,k,\epsilon,B}}{\sqrt T}\right\},\qquad C_{d,k,\epsilon,B}=\frac{1024B d^{dk}}{\epsilon}.\] The implication imposes no lower bound on any coordinate of \(q\) and no contraction condition on \(L_q\).
statements.justification: This conditional implication states the dimension-explicit sample-length certificate delivered only after the mandatory square and whole-polytope obligations are resolved.
statements.gap: HaughSingal2026Casino, arXiv version 3, pages 9--11, Sections 4.2--4.3, shows only that in its special casino model the time-homogeneous and time-inhomogeneous \(\mathrm{EWAC}/T\) bounds converge together as \(T\to\infty\); it supplies neither a finite root-\(T\) rate nor a bound uniform over the complete finite-state stationary response-program fiber. LallyKazemiPaoletti2026RobustCounterfactualMDP is sharp one transition at a time, HaughSingal2023DynamicLatent gives finite-record programs, and SayedanaCainesMahajan2025 controls one fixed kernel; none supplies the stated whole-polytope premise.
statements.consumer: An affirmative open-question result turns this implication into a sample-length certificate for robust trajectory attribution and policy auditing.

statements.statement: The construction \(\mathfrak W_{\mathrm{bin}}\) belongs to \(\mathfrak M_{2,2,T}(1/4,2)\); every one of the sixteen response programs has mass at least \(1/128\) under each of \(q_+\) and \(q_-\), and \[Q^{\mathrm{full}}_{q_+,T}(X_{0:T})-Q^{\mathrm{full}}_{q_-,T}(X_{0:T})=\frac{1}{2T}\sum_{j=1}^T\bigl(1-2^{-(T-j+1)}\bigr)(2X_j-1).\] With the identity observation map, \(E_T=X_{0:T}\), and consequently \(\liminf_{T\to\infty}\sqrt T\,\mathbb E_{\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}}[D_T(P,\rho,b,o,E_T)]\ge1/\sqrt{2\pi}\). Thus no uniform upper rate on this model class can be \(o(T^{-1/2})\), even on a full-support region of response laws.
statements.justification: A legal full-support feedback construction rules out any uniformly faster ambiguity rate and shows that the boundary phenomenon is not driven by zero response masses.
statements.gap: The one-transition bounds in LallyKazemiPaoletti2026RobustCounterfactualMDP and the special-casino qualitative convergence of time-homogeneous and time-inhomogeneous \(\mathrm{EWAC}/T\) bounds in HaughSingal2026Casino do not give a lower-rate witness for recursive stationary-feedback counterfactuals.
statements.consumer: Study designers learn that doubling counterfactual precision can require approximately four times the factual record length even under benign nominal transitions.

statements.statement: Suppose each transition row has \(n_{x,a}\) independent multinomial calibration draws, the nominal zero pattern is known, and calibration is independent of the factual record. Then \[\Pr_{\mathrm{cal}}\left\{I_T(P,\rho,b,o,e)\subseteq\widehat I_{T,\alpha}(P,\rho,b,o,e)\text{ for every }T\ge1\text{ and every }e\in\mathcal O^{T+1}\text{ with }\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}(E_T=e)>0\right\}\ge1-\alpha.\] Both coarsened-record endpoints are therefore covered simultaneously for every fixed factual-law-positive record, even when response masses are zero and the endpoint-active face changes.
statements.justification: Set inversion delivers honest endpoint coverage under the explicitly indexed factual law without differentiating a nonunique optimizer or excluding response-polytope boundaries.
statements.gap: KaidoMolinariStoye2019CalibratedProjection gives uniform asymptotic projection inference for moment models, while LallyKazemiPaoletti2026RobustCounterfactualMDP explicitly leaves estimated transition laws open; neither provides this exact simultaneous stationary-response fiber.
statements.consumer: An analyst with independent simulator or calibration transitions can attach a finite-sample confidence statement to the sharp coarsened-record counterfactual interval.

sampling_model.design: One stationary iid-response SCM generates the factual record; an independent generative calibration experiment supplies rowwise multinomial draws.
sampling_model.units: The causal query concerns one unit observed for \(T\) transitions; calibration units are independent across draws and rows.
sampling_model.treatment: The factual and alternative interventions are the fixed stationary policies \(b\) and \(\pi\).
sampling_model.overlap: Known nominal support with \(P(y\mid x,a)\ge\epsilon\) on each positive cell; no response-program mass is bounded away from zero.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The controlled transition law is either known or estimated by \(\widehat P\) from independent rowwise multinomial calibration samples; no trajectory-only nuisance estimator is claimed.

estimand_functional: \([\min_{q\in\Theta(P)}Q_{q,T}(P,\rho,b,o,e),\max_{q\in\Theta(P)}Q_{q,T}(P,\rho,b,o,e)]\), with one stationary response-mass vector shared across every date and hidden branch

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 4.1--4.3 give exact closed-form lower and upper bounds for one counterfactual transition after one observed transition.
Theorem 2.4, Proposition 2.5, and Theorem 2.8 reduce finite discrete counterfactual bounds to optimization over a complete canonical SCM family.
The average-reward results derive concentration for one fixed policy and kernel from a Poisson-equation martingale decomposition.
In the paper's special casino model, the time-homogeneous and time-inhomogeneous \(\mathrm{EWAC}/T\) bounds converge together as \(T\to\infty\) (arXiv version 3, pages 9--11, Sections 4.2--4.3).
The paper constructs uniformly asymptotically valid confidence intervals for smooth projections of moment-identified parameter sets.
The paper generates individual POMDP counterfactual trajectories after selecting the Gumbel-Max SCM and proves its counterfactual-stability property.
The paper gives exact polynomial-program bounds for a terminal counterfactual probability in a dynamic latent-state model with time-invariant response distributions.
Theorems 2 and 4 control martingale-process suprema through sequential Rademacher complexity and sequential covering integrals.
Section 2 represents causal mechanisms as implicit couplings, while Propositions 1--2 establish limitations of fixed implicit couplings.
Theorems 12.8 and 14.7 derive self-normalized maximal and vector-martingale inequalities by exponential mixing.
Uniform observability guarantees nonlinear-filter stability without stability assumptions on the hidden signal.
The paper derives forgetting of an HMM filter from explicit coupling conditions on posterior kernels.
Section 5 gives an efficient influence function and an efficient asymptotically normal estimator for worst-case value under multiplicative transition perturbations.

tldr: A known finite controlled transition law does not identify the same unit's counterfactual trajectory because it leaves the response-program coupling unspecified. The closest long-record comparator shows only that, in a special casino model, time-homogeneous and time-inhomogeneous \(\mathrm{EWAC}/T\) bounds converge together as \(T\to\infty\); it gives neither a finite root-\(T\) rate nor a bound uniform over the complete finite-state stationary response-program fiber. Under the explicitly induced factual law \(\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}\), the field-level kernel asks whether the expected diameter of the sharp coarsened-record average-reward interval contracts at the root-\(T\) rate uniformly over that complete fiber, without positive response masses or contraction of conditional counterfactual kernels. The first D0 obligation is the synchronizer--two-permutation square: it must yield a uniform two-parameter root-\(T\) bound or an explicit horizon-dependent counterselection with the sharp replacement rate. Only an affirmative square-to-polytope maximal inequality activates the conditional \(1024B d^{dk}/(\epsilon\sqrt T)\) width theorem. A stationary shared-response endpoint proposition supplies infrastructure, while a full-support root-\(T\) lower witness and simultaneous finite-sample confidence-fiber coverage complete the proposal.

project_justification.gap: Published SCM work supplies selected-mechanism trajectories, exact one-step compatible-coupling bounds, or generic finite canonical programs. The closest long-record result, HaughSingal2026Casino, shows only that in its special casino model the time-homogeneous and time-inhomogeneous \(\mathrm{EWAC}/T\) bounds converge together as \(T\to\infty\). It gives neither a finite root-\(T\) rate nor a bound uniform over the complete finite-state stationary response-program fiber, while average-reward concentration supplies a Poisson martingale only for one fixed kernel.
project_justification.niche: The missing field-level object beyond that qualitative special-casino limit is a finite-horizon uniform maximal inequality for posterior-normalized Poisson martingales indexed by the complete response polytope, including zero-mass faces and noncontracting conditional kernels. The synchronizer--two-permutation square is the decisive first interior-face test.
project_justification.fill: The project first resolves that square by a uniform root-rate bound or a sharp horizon-dependent counterselection, then conditionally propagates an affirmative bound to the whole finite-state stationary response-program polytope and an explicit finite root-\(T\) expected-width theorem. This directly supplies the rate and uniformity absent from the special-casino asymptotic comparison. Full-record and coarsened-record functionals are kept separate under \(\Pr_{P,\rho,b,o}\); stationary endpoint attainment, a full-support lower construction, and simultaneous calibration-set inversion are supporting components.

The synchronizer--two-permutation square in \texttt{def:triangle-handle} is the first D0 obligation: it must produce a uniform two-parameter root-\(T\) bound or an explicit horizon-dependent counterselection and sharp replacement rate. honest_scope: The root-\(T\) whole-polytope inequality and its explicit constant are open, so \texttt{thm:root-t-width} is only an implication from an affirmative resolution of \texttt{oeq:polytope-maximal-inequality}.
